title: Tuesday · maths, Health, French and Nevermoor
arrival: Answer attendance, then hand in forms. Get paper and a pencil ready for maths.
note: Start with order of operations and continue the existing Class Game Afternoon task. Use the rest of the morning work block for unfinished maths or existing portfolio work. After recess, practise feelings, needs and boundaries with a fictional situation. French is 12:35–1:35, followed by a quiet reset and Nevermoor from the actual class bookmark. Finish with a short work-and-tidy block. Keep snack at 10:20, recess 10:35–10:50, lunch 11:50–12:35 and dismissal at 2:35. Check what students actually need to finish; this plan adds no new homework or posting deadline.

blocks.title: Maths · order of operations
blocks.notes: Use 20–30 minutes for a model and discussion, then continue the existing Class Game Afternoon task. First check the current stopping point and what students can already explain. Prompt: Our class has $60. We buy 4 packs of game cards at $6 each and 3 packs of pencils at $4 each. Share the money left equally between 2 activity stations. How much does each station receive? Model [60 − (4 × 6 + 3 × 4)] ÷ 2: purchases cost $24 + $12 = $36; $24 remains, so each station receives $12. Explain what each part means and record one step per line. Accept equivalent correct expressions, such as (60 − 4 × 6 − 3 × 4) ÷ 2. Work within brackets first, including multiplication before addition; multiplication/division share priority and go left to right, as do addition/subtraction. Ask students to explain why dividing the whole $60 first would not describe this situation. Continue the already-assigned task and use an explanation of the first step as a quick understanding check. Do not turn the teacher model into a claim of independent assessment evidence. Paper and a board provide the complete route; an existing MathUP example is optional support.

studentSteps: Find the cost of the cards and pencils.

blocks.title: Health · feelings, needs and boundaries
blocks.notes: Use the existing agreements and feelings/needs visuals; start with what the class has actually discussed. Keep one manageable fictional scenario: two friends want to play different games. Model a possible feeling (disappointed), a need (choice or belonging) and a respectful request ('Could we take turns choosing?'). These are possibilities, not guesses about a real person's feelings. Explore another strategy, such as agreeing on a different game. Link to using words carefully and checking assumptions where useful, without making the Agreements rules that excuse harm. A request allows a no; respect personal space and stop signals. Students may speak, draw, point, write, observe or pass on performance. Ask for one possible feeling/need, one request and what to do if the answer is no. No personal conflict or sensitive disclosure is required. For unsafe situations, step away and seek a trusted adult; a perfect sentence is not required. Use the existing poster/PDF and paper response; no new Health upload is assigned.
blocks.firstAction: Look at the fictional situation and notice a possible feeling and need.
studentSteps: Listen to the made-up situation about choosing a game.
Suggest a feeling and a need; more than one answer may fit.
Say, draw or write a respectful request and another way to solve the problem.
Explain how to respect a no or stop.

blocks.title: English Language Arts · Nevermoor
blocks.notes: Continue Nevermoor from the actual class bookmark. Briefly recall the last part actually read; do not invent story events or assume a chapter is finished. Read or listen, identify a character or setting detail, and give an idea supported by that detail. If it fits the passage actually read, compare what has changed and stayed the same in the character's life. Treat death/rebirth as a literary interpretation, not a required belief or personal disclosure. Accept other interpretations supported by story evidence.

studentSteps: Read or listen from our actual stopping point.

Mark where we stop and keep one question for next time.
